items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I was affiliated with a gentleman named Lew Futterman that had a publishing company.

ctx.x: And gosh, you made quite a bit of music with Jack McDuff.

Oh yeah. Jack and I met in Chicago because he lived there at the time. And he had a small band that we used to work with and rehearse. So that was my first time playing with Jack. And then when I came to New York and Jack came through I was affiliated with a gentleman named Lew Futterman that had a publishing company. So he would record a lot of the songs in the publishing company. And so McDuff recorded about three or four songs of mine, and then I recorded some other music. I had quite a few other songs that…
Yeah, you’ve done quite a bit of writing. Do you sit at a keyboard when you write? Or how does it evolve? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-
